# `silk/crypto/sha1`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compute SHA-1 digests (20 bytes) for old protocols and file formats.

## When to use
Use [`Sha1`](#Sha1) only when an existing format needs SHA-1, such as a Git object ID or the WebSocket
handshake. For new designs, use SHA-256 from `silk.crypto.sha2` or SHA-3 from `silk.crypto.sha3`. For the keys
of a hash map, use `silk.collections.hash`.

## Details
[`Sha1.hash`](#Sha1.impl.hash) returns the digest of one slice. For a message that arrives in parts, call
[`Sha1.make`](#Sha1.impl.make), then [`Sha1.update`](#Sha1.impl.update) for each part, then [`Sha1.finish`](#Sha1.impl.finish). Nothing allocates.

## Gotchas
SHA-1 is broken: an attacker can make two different messages with the same digest. Do not use it
for signatures, certificates, or checks against tampering.

## Examples
### Hash a message in one call and in parts
```silk
import silk.crypto.sha1 { Sha1 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let oneShot = Sha1.hash(b"abc")
  let mut state = Sha1.make()
  state.update(b"a")
  state.update(b"bc")
  let streamed = state.finish()

  // SHA-1("abc") is a9993e36...d89d.
  if oneShot[0] != 0xa9 || oneShot[19] != 0x9d || streamed[0] != oneShot[0] {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Sha1` with `import silk.crypto.sha1 { Sha1 }`.

## `Sha1`

```silk
pub struct Sha1
```

A streaming SHA-1 state that returns a 20-byte digest.

Call [`Sha1.update`](#Sha1.impl.update) for each part of the message, then [`Sha1.finish`](#Sha1.impl.finish). The state is a
fixed-size value and does not allocate.

### Gotchas
SHA-1 is broken. Use it only where an existing format needs it.

<a id="Sha1.impl.update"></a>

### Method `update`

```silk
pub fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to the end of the message.

Any split of the message into parts gives the same digest. An empty slice changes nothing.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if the full message is longer than 2^64 - 1 bits.

<a id="Sha1.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self) -> [u8; 20]
```

Returns the 20-byte SHA-1 digest of the message and consumes the state.

pub fn hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> [u8; 20]

Returns the 20-byte SHA-1 digest of `bytes`.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `bytes` is longer than 2^64 - 1 bits.
